It's ridiculously repetitive... even for a Survivors-style game. You can have 4 weapons and 4 passives. The passives aren't interesting and neither are the weapons except for maybe one or two; all you do is upgrade these 8 stats over and over and over by the smallest amounts; there are no weapon synergies or evolutions. Maps are boring. Enemies are boring... ...This game is just really really bad, even as a an early acces title. This could be an extremely early tech-demo at best, but even then it looks like it is fundamentally flawed. Play literally any other Survivors-style game instead.

Not to bad for day 1 of a Reverse Bullet Hell style game. I would say its middle of the pack as far as Vamprie Survival style games go. The controls are decent, gameplay is fun and there are a few new aspects they bring to the table. Also the setting is good. But there are some issues, the game sort of has a bland look to it, I hope the overall art design is improved during the Early Access period. Also we need more choices for what abilities to pick when we level up, just more variety. I like that you can pick a companion to rip around with you to, it works well in this setting and this genre. Work on the art design and more content and you should have a good VS like game here. The Pathfinder setting is great for this style of game, take your time and keep improving things each update. I would say buy Halls of Torment instead of this if you don't own that, as its in a little better shape atm, but the same style of fantasy setting. Buy it down the road after a few content updates, unless you need a new VS style game right now for your steam deck, then pick it up now. Good chill fun, but not quite all the way there yet, but well on its way. This has become a genre I really like to play on my steam deck and it works great on there like most the others in this genre do. It is a pretty good start so far, but I would suggest Vampire Survivors, Army of Ruin, Nordic Ashes and Halls Of Torment before this game as they have more content. But if you want another one to play and see how it gets developed, by all means pick this up, if not wait a few months. The game also is one that for me atleast, took awhile to click. Usually thee Bullet Hell games click instantly but this took an hour or 2 to learn the ins and outs of. Its also improved a pretty decent amount with updates. Looking forward to the future, this is a good start.

I want to start this review by saying this game is absolutely worth watching grow. It has a ton of potential to eventually be a fun and unique experience in this genre. That being said, these games generally launch with several characters to prevent boring and repetitive gameplay. This one launched with three and two of them don't play all that different from one another unless you're willing to dedicate several hours to leveling them. Which brings me to the next major issue, progression is incredibly slow. I've put nearly 20 hours in and feel like I've accomplished next to nothing so far. The best way to grind XP is by completing quests and you can only have three at a time, so if you want to grind XP quickly it's often a better idea to complete your quests and duck out of your current run to grab that XP and get three new quests. Right now I'd say the game really needs more character classes with vastly different playstyles to help break up the monotony of gameplay. Giving the Fighter and Rogue clearer identities at lower levels would also help out a lot. Speeding up progression would be great, but it won't solve the problem of each run feeling the same with we're stuck with effectively two different characters.

Mediocre game plagued by questionable, out of touch design choices. -Your companion feels just barely better than useless -Your companion can't get any upgrades -The RPG element to character design is underwhelming and weakly implemented -"Weapon" choices are extremely limited, both in quantity and by what's equippable -Talents/Character attributes are painfully incremental, boring, and low impact -Leveling up your character is horrifically slow, probably to pad out the amount of time it would take to win a run -The game limits how strong your abilities can become, [b]eventually taking away the possibility to level up[/b], which eventaully makes one of the five available potions useless -The quests offered feel very low effort and unrewarding -Playing as the wizard and completing a run, by the end I was pretty much unable to see anything on the screen. The wizard can unleash up to 13 massive meteors with the right upgrades, which absolutely dominate mobs, but also literally smoke up the entire screen completely removing all visibility. The AOE cone of cold spell, howling frost, is similar. -The "weapon" balance is... poor. Passives within the run are also not balanced, some are extremely impactful, some are completely useless. I feel bad for anyone who takes extra essence (extra experience) when the game completely removes the ability to level up if you plan and play well enough. -The wizard is probably the only character that can complete a run before level 3. -Some may disagree, but the die rolls on the chests just don't feel great. The game isn't good enough for me to care to actually track the die rolls, but there were a disproportionate amount of 1-4 rolls IMO. Far more than 17-20 over the course of ~8 hours, especially on the boss chests which contain better loot. -Many attacks and death effects by enemies are untelegraphed and unavoidable, especially with the amount of screen clutter from your character's "weapons". -The bosses feel like HP sponges, and are not that enjoyable. The best approach is to have as much damage as possible, but the game removes your ability to increase your damage (your weapon maxes out). -I saw the warriors sword get an extra swing at max level, but lack of evolutions or any benefit to maxing out a weapon (which probably shouldn't happen) is extremely unsatisfying -Enemies (eventually) popping out of thin air and spawning on top of your character is poor design that many developers have learned to avoid, not in this game -The story, lore, and writing are weak and not fleshed out, understandable for an early access rogue-like -Many of the tooltips for "weapons" are incorrect, for instance the gauntlet says it pulls enemies in when it in fact pushes enemies away, the bow says it fires in a random direction when it fires in a clockwise cardinal direction pattern, and some wizard spells say they fire in a random direction, but they target a random enemy. -Most "weapons" are extremely underpowered without meta-progression or level-locked passives -The cost to upgrade potions is insane. You could probably put hundreds of hours into the game and not be able to upgrade them all to the incrementally small "max" In summary, the game plays like a predatory incremental mobile game without the cash grab. It feels like the developers are trying to pad out the game by making it impossible to progress without grinding. It's less of a game when skill and knowledge aren't what grant success, but grinding out small and boring upgrades and being allowed to choose impactful passives after grinding out some levels are what allow success.

Bought this game on sale and to show my appreciation for Pathfinder, and booted it up just to see what it was like for a quick session. Check the clock and it's been nearly 3 hours. So, I do recommend at this point, and look forward to the future additions to the game. Pros: Difficulty scales well with the play style and doesn't get stale; some stages are easier with different builds Builds are fun and offer a lot to play around with; it's easy to be as overpowered but still face challenges Instructions on how to play are very transparent Skills boosts are noticeable in power-ups Cons: Despite build variety, some skills are too powerful not to pick for your character Some skills aren't easily able to see when they are active (a lot of shield skills, Fireball the spell of all things, and some skill triggers are unnoticeable during the heat of battle making it difficult to see if your build is working properly) A few bugs on the controller support

While ok the game still needs a lot of work, primarilly in conveying information and secondly in making more intressting content. Currently several uppgrades feels meaningless because there's no reference point. What does 1, 10 or 0.1 armour mean? What about Block? Does it even do anything? Right now only God knows that. Character specific progression like Stats and Talents have potential but is hamstrung by by information blockage and basic nature. +stat or +%stat aren't all that interessting. About the cards that gives meta progression: A better system would be gear like in Death Must Die. In it's present card form the meta grind feels flat and unsatisfying, lacking all the exitement that it could have. Edit: The environmental attacks that come in from offscreen just feels dumb. There's too many from too many angles to effectively dodge and they can't be mitigated by removing their source so all that's left is to face-tank them. Very unsatisfying mechanic.

This game left behind an empty feeling behind after playing for several hours. First of all the only things that seem to link this to Pathfinder are: the setting (unimportant since its just a paper thin excuse plot), the fact the the three classes are playable in Pathfinder (an in name only resemblance), and there is a D20 that is used at some point it time. That is it. Second thing to note is that the progression system is pretty uninteresting. Instead of leveling and getting interesting feats from Pathfinder to change up your playstyle you get skills that give pretty minor bonuses and are similar to progression boosts you would see in tens of other Survivor type games. There are card drops during runs that need gold to activate for very minor boosts such as a +1% damage against skeletons or chest unlocks 0.5% faster. And there are potions that cost absurd amounts of gold to unlock and that I cant really tell the difference between in game since they come in 3 different colors despite multiple different potions (I just pick it up and assume it does something slightly beneficial). The thing that this Survivors game does different in anyway is that you choose a companion to adventure with you. In practice this means they do a very meager amount of damage and get some experience towards their level progression. If you are looking for a vampire survivors style game there are a great many that do a better job than this one and if you are looking for a Pathfinder video game there are much better options. Hopefully the game will improve in time but until then you are safe skipping this one.

This is a great game in the bullet hell/ Vampire Survivors clone genre. It is basically Dungeons and Dragons meets Vampire Survivors. Well, technically it is Pathfinder, which is a copy of D&D 3 edition, but who cares... The game is really good even at this early state of development. Nice graphics, and lots of builds. I actually enjoyed it a lot. I think it needs more classes, weapons, stages, though. And it needs to tone down the upgrades a little, there are too many upgrades, both in-stage and permanent upgrades, too much grind to unlock them all. Otherwise, it is good. I like it. If you are not tired of Vampire Survivor clones yet, you should get it, it is cheap. It also plays excellently on Linux with Proton.

My review may change after future updates and rebalancing, but the game doesn't feel complete. The bonuses you get to your weapons and your passives are very small and don't feel like they are making a difference. I hate that most passives don't seem to affect your attacks in any way. Passives like more potions, more chests, and more XP, those are fine but what about a passive that gives increased attack for all weapons or increased projectile speed for all attacks? As it stands, the most effective build is as simple as grab the attacks that do the most damage and grab all the defensive passives. Then there is the leveling system. On paper, it seems pretty cool. You have your core stats; Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma. As you level up by playing the game over and over, you are able to increase these stats which affect things like weapon damage, cooldown, and attack range. The problem is, the bonuses are so small that I never noticed a difference. The good thing is they let you reset your stats and spend your points for free whenever you want. The bad thing is they limit you so that you can't stat dump into a single skill. Also the dice rolls for loot feel rigged. In the first hour I played the game, I felt like I was rolling higher. 15-20 a lot of the time. In the later hours, I would be lucky to roll above 10. It becomes very apparent it is rigged when you go for the "Lucky" passive ability which increases your chance of finding a treasure chest. If you max that ability out, you find chests left and right, but your rolls for loot are almost always going to be below 10. It really feels like any time I think of something that would make my playthrough more enjoyable, the devs already thought of it and they blocked you from doing it. This game has a lot of potential to be fun, but it needs a lot more content, and the devs need to let the players have more power, even if they are breaking the game in the process. I have tried to give my review without bringing up Vampire Survivors, but I need to make a point. In VS, you start off a run weak, maybe getting overwhelmed a bit. But with the right combination of abilities, by the end of a run you become an unkillable god. Now to contrast that, in Gallowspire Survivors you start the run weak, maybe getting overwhelmed a bit. But with the right combination of abilities, by the end of the run you are weak and maybe getting overwhelmed a bit. You never have that satisfying payoff The game needs some good updates to be truly fun.

Despite earlier negative reviews, this game is now patched and a blast. The initial reviews kept me away, but a recent patch with positive reviews, in addition to a nice sale, enabled me to purchase this. Overall, the game is a blast. Nothing groundbreaking, but the visuals and performance are great on a handheld and you have a constant sense of progression. Through each run you have a clear upgrade/improvement of your character, so you never feel as though you are wasting your time. The UX when upgrading your character(s) between matches could use some improvement, and that is its biggest determent, but other than that I had no issues. Highly recommend for fans of the genre.

Felt compelled to write a review for the first time. This game gets a lot of bad reviews and I don't understand why. Some reviews were posted after ten minutes of playtime?! Just like with all of these games, you need to upgrade your abilities before you can have any sort of fun. It's not the best or most innovative of the genre, but it is definitely fun. The game is very well polished for EA, and I enjoy how it breaks runs up into different floors of around 4 minutes each. You can focus more on farming than just plain surviving hordes. The upgrades are very small, but just like with all of these types of games, repeat the first level a few times to upgrade your abilities, and it becomes very manageable. The feature of running with a companion is one that I like and not found in many of these types of games. The sound, music, voiceover, and graphics are all very good. You can choose fro male or female characters, and customize their names. Some bad reviews mentioned not being anything at all like the Pathfinder tabletop rpg. I've only played that a few times and stopped once DND5e was released, but I still can't really see why this is a reason to not recommend. It's not meant to be a Pathfinder sim--there are great games that do that already. Anyway, I gave this game a try during the spring sale and I'm glad I did. Again, it's not Halls of Torment or VS, but what is? It's an entertaining addition to the genre and worth the play if it's on sale. The price is a bit higher than many superior games in the genre, so perhaps that's why the game is getting more negative reviews than I think it deserves. It's still in EA and Pathfinder is a strong brand, so hopefully the devs add more classes than the 3 you can choose from. I will say it does play better on steamdeck than PC as it's easier to aim with the twin stick.

The game has a lot of systems for upgrading. They are mostly stat upgrades which I don't mind, but it would be nice if there were some that did more than stats. The companion is also neat. Unfortunately though, everything feels insignificant and pointless. The whole game is completely forgettable. You could play for an hour straight and barely remember playing at all. You get skills and passives and upgrade them during your runs, but all runs feel the same because they all feel like nothing. It's like playing a fighting game but every hit has 0 impact. Sure, it still damages the enemy, but there's no reaction, no sense of actually hitting them. This makes the game very boring. Worse yet, on only the 3rd stage of the 2nd area, I began having major frame rate issues. I've played tons of these types of games and never had problems. So to have them with this game without that much even going on is pitiful. It's sad because I think this game does have some neat mechanics like the companion and upgrade system. However, it's just not worth it. Maybe co-op is better, but I highly doubt it.

Good enough for $4 for 9 hours of gameplay that I'll play more of. I *am* already worried about longevity and build variety, however. The amount of upgrades and metaprogression is great, and there's enough goals that the fact that most of the upgrades are "just" % stat boosts is fine. There's even cool Pathfinder monster art I recognize as a 2e player, though I can't speak to the story besides broad strokes "makes sense enough". But there's basically two types of attacks - spells (of 3 elements, which do encourage synergies) and weapons, and based on playing just Fighter and Wizard I feel like there's not much left over for the Rogue to be unique -- I did one run with them and found out they use almost all the same weapons as Fighter besides Dagger and maybe something else. There's not much Martial build synergy besides "build damage" or "build defenses", so you just pick whichever attacks you like the most or do the most damage -- I haven't seen weapon+weapon specializations yet after starting the third map, though for practical purposes "melee" vs "ranged" is a build choice as you grind your Fighter right next to mobs or stay away (preliminary results is Ranged is just better and Great Axe + Crossbow + Bow + Chakram might be the braindead pick every run). You also only level 1.5 characters per run (your main character and partially your companion), so one character is inevitably left to rot until you do low level runs as the maps' difficulty scales fairly fast compared to other Survivors games; there's an exponential amount of ranged enemies compared to 20 Minutes to Dawn. There's still 4 difficulties and 2 maps for me to beat, as well as tons of cards (permanent stat upgrades for all characters) to find. The characters scale all the way to lv20 while I'm level 5 at this point in the review.

Okay. I really, really wanted to like this one because I love Pathfinder. Every time I tried it during the EA period it seemed unpolished, unfinished, and most of all boring, but that was EA, right? Now we are at 1.0 and... it still feels unpolished, unfinished, and boring. The designers seem to fail both at making a good swarm survivor game and at making it feel even remotely like a Pathfinder game. Unless they change things up HEAVILY it is not really worth playing even for people like me who have already 100% Vampire Survivors and the other good ones in the genre and are looking for a new fix. This one just is not it.

The game is fun, but still kind of feel like early access due to its lack of build diversity and overall things to do in the game. The overall loop of grinding to get levels is nice, since there are no Survivors-like games that have a traditional level grind outside of the game. This aspect is greatly appreciated, and I think can be improved upon a lot as well. My suggestions for this game: 1) Increase build diversity -- This can be done by just adding more skills and maybe add some unique talents that can modify attacks and abilities and the way they are used. 2) Skill evolutions - The fact that you aren't rewarded for maxing a skill out feels bad. I should be able to dictate the way I want to play the run out to a certain degree. It's going to be RNG dependant on your skill choices given either way, but there should be an incentive to max out a certain skill rather than just getting a skill to 70-80% then working on the weaker skills. 3) Movement speed is rampant - The game feels kind of janky with how easily I can just zoom across the map. I sometimes get so fast that I end up crashing into monsters not matter how good my build gets. I don't know what you can do, but the game feels cheaper with how fast and how accessible it is to just become a bullet train. 4) More meta-grind: While the level grind is fine, and so are the character specific upgrades as well, but I feel like there should be some kind of equipment put into the game as well. The game already has a feel of Death Must Die, so why not play into it? Have it be ARPG style so you can fish for legendaries/unique equipment, so each and every run has the potential to have crazy rewards. 5) More characters - I'm sure you are already working on this in some sort of fashion so it's not a big deal, just my two cents. 6) Experiment with the way percentages work on your skills. You guys have implemented a unique take on levelling skills. No other rogue-like uses skill upgrades in a percentage. Again, I don't know what you can do with this, but it's definitely something a good dev can make even better. Overall, I think that the game is worth the price even though there are survivors-likes out there with more to the game. If you continue to upgrade the game I will keep this as a positive review, however, if you do not, then I cannot recommend this as an unfinished product.

The game has little to no content. Only 3 classes (with no incentive to switch between them since you will want to just minmax a single character), and only 4 levels with near identical monsters (there are just melee, ranged and explodey ones) where the only variation is given by the bosses. After that the only thing you can do is play again and again with a higher "difficulty" which just makes monsters do more damage and have more hp. The only meta progression once you get the talents you want is only inflating your characters' stats more and more to catch up with the higher difficulties. Even for the 4 € I paid for it, it wasn't worth it. The game is pratty uninspired.

Alright. [i]Pathfinder: Gallowspire Survivors[/i] is what I'd describe as a [b]meh out of 10[/b] type of game. It doesn't do anything specifically poorly, but it doesn't really excel at anything either. It's fun for a minute but loses its charm quickly. With that in mind, let's dive in: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3275681916 This game is really two things: a Pathfinder licensed game and a VS-like (auto battler). If the devs removed the word Pathfinder from the title, you would absolutely never know it was a licensed game in the Pathfinder IP. There's nothing in the game that truly makes it Pathfinder. It IS functionally a Survivors game, but it does nothing noteworthy at all to set itself apart from other entries in any way shape or form. In fact, I'd say the cool things that you'd come to expect from a Survivors title are absent here. For example, while in the arenas, and as you upgrade find and your skills, there are only buffs to said skills available. There is no tiered system wherein you earn special abilities when reaching certain upgrade levels. It's just straight buffs all the time. After you leave a run, you can upgrade your character, artifacts found in your runs, potions, and your bestiary. This latter part is probably the only unique thing about the game, inasmuch as you can use gold to give yourself nominal buffs for fighting or defending against certain enemies by upgrading that enemy type in your bestiary. The same is true for upgrading artifacts. Upgrading your character is a matter of gaining points to upgrade your classic d20 ability scores. Which you will be min/maxing in this game. Potion upgrades are the only thing in the game where it can change what the item or ability actually does. For example, you can upgrade a health potion to also offer a regenerate property. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3275926797 While in runs, the lack of any special upgrade tiers is kind of uninspiring. Imagine, if you will, that you're playing through a tabletop campaign, and you find a +1 longsword. Cool. It's definitely better than your plain old non-magical sword. But is it as cool as finding a +1 Luckblade, Flaming Sword, an Intelligent +1 Sword, etc...? No, no it's not. It's an upgrade but doesn't offer any sort of wow factor. And to me, that lack of wow factor is pervasive in this game. The combat is fun enough, but it always feels a bit lackluster. And the visuals do this no favors. They look okay, but again, there's no 'holy s%^&' moments. It's just stuff happening on screen. Enemies aren't particularly noteworthy except bosses and bosses don't really feature any kind of interesting move set. If anything, they tend to err on the side of annoyingly spamming one ability. The audio tracks are okay, but not particularly memorable either. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3275681895 Is this an actual bad game? No. It is competent in everything it does. But the Pathfinder is notably absent and it lacks any gameplay features that really have me wanting to keep coming back to this over and over. Why keep playing this when I can literally fire up Vampire Survivors, which costs less, is innovative, and adds cool new things to the base game on the regular? This game's lackluster nature is inarguably its greatest flaw. There are a lot of missed opportunities with this title. Is it worth a look? With a hefty discount, sure. But don't have high expectations with this game. I'll be giving this a positive rating since there's no neutral rating and it's not a bad game, but holy meh! A lot of thinking is not required, just get in, get used to the idea that you don't activate weapons, they shoot on their own, and have a blast. And THEN take the wizard, start a darkest dungeon run, spec him in fire magic, and see ABSOLUTELY NOTHING on the screen due to all the effects :)

I have actually been enjoying the game myself. The new modes have added that extra layer of difficulty that's for sure. Having to rank up a second character along with your main one is a nice challenge and one that gets easier as I go. One thing I really appreciate the devs added was the different defense options you can trigger when you need them during battle. Loot for ranking seems to be setup pretty well too with several upgrade areas for you to increase your power, resilience, and healing. Also, the addition of the card collection in-game for ranking up makes it even more is enjoyable since after collecting you can purchase that cards strength with gold. Here's to hoping the dev team will continue to show love to this game over time because there is a some solid game time to be had in this title. If you like action roguelikes then this is a must buy, especially at such a low price point.
